summary: An LTP client holds an instrument and a Quote client asks for it: the broker refuses the Quote code, so the Quote client is told why and the LTP code is not released, so the LTP client keeps streaming (review X2).

notes: The web sends the new code and keeps the old ones per client; it logs a refused REST subscribe and acknowledges it (compositedge_websocket.py:289-292), a web defect the desktop does not copy (review R107-03). The desktop's upgrade order (the new code first, the old released once it is taken) is its own, so a refusal leaves the holder streaming.
The refusal's code and description are made up: no recorded XTS refusal exists.

deviations.reason: The web sends XTS's LastTradedTime as it comes, seconds since 1980-01-01 IST (1478686530 is 2026-11-09 10:15:30 IST): a wrong unit, since feed timestamps are Unix epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends the trade time in milliseconds (1794199530000).
